page: Amazon Web Services i4i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. This configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The instance includes 937 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1890.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1590.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3856.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3429.0. Memory bandwidth is also on the lower end, with read-only large block bandwidth at 29.32 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 24.65 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average performance in encryption tests and static web serving throughput, but shows weaker results in database operations and Redis SET operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4i.xlarge offers a high ratio of local NVMe SSD storage and memory relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized option for storage-heavy workloads rather than compute-intensive tasks. The tradeoff lies in its modest multi-core processing and memory bandwidth performance. This instance is best suited for workloads requiring fast local storage access and moderate memory capacity, such as small-scale transactional databases, NoSQL databases, and web serving applications with local caching needs.
